# Headless-Chrome acceptance suite for the browser extension (issue #23):
# builds the extension zip, runs the Node vm-sandbox unit tests, then the
# Dart integration suite (test/browser_ext/, `integration` tag) against a
# real headless Chrome. Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Browser extension

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'
      - 'lib/src/browser/**'
      - 'bin/serve_bridge.dart'
      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'
      - 'lib/src/browser/**'
      - 'bin/serve_bridge.dart'
      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (issue #194 pt 5, same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Browser extension-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  headless-suite:
    name: Headless Chrome suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # Chrome for Testing, NOT branded google-chrome-stable: branded builds
      # silently ignore --load-extension (removed mid-2025), and the whole
      # suite drives the extension through that flag.
      - name: Install Chrome for Testing
        id: chrome
        run: |
          npx -y @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft"
          echo "chrome-path=$(find "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft" -name chrome -type f | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # browser_ext/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root), so
      # its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: Dart unit tests (browser_ext/dart)
        run: cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # Compiles the embedded agent (dart2js, fails loudly on errors) and
      # zips the runtime files — the artifact under test AND the AC11 upload.
      - name: Build extension
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh

      # Node 22's `node --test` does not glob arguments itself; bash expands
      # the pattern (or pass the directory: node --test browser_ext/test/).
      - name: Node unit tests (vm sandbox)
        run: node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs

      # -j 1: every test spawns its own Chrome; parallel workers on one
      # runner fight over CPU and the DevTools handshakes get flaky.
      - name: Dart integration suite (headless Chrome)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
        run: dart test test/browser_ext/ -j 1 --tags integration

      # Playwright drives the SAME unpacked extension in the SAME Chrome for
      # Testing build (issue #34 item 2). npm ci needs the committed
      # package-lock.json; the agent.js build above satisfies global-setup.
      # FA_E2E_CI opts the SW-residency spec in (real idle shutdown + alarm
      # revival — too wall-clock-flaky for dev machines).
      - name: Playwright e2e (extension, real Chrome)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
          FA_E2E_CI: '1'
        run: |
          cd browser_ext/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload extension zip (AC11)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-extension
          path: build/fa-extension.zip

  # Manual variant only: rebuilds the extension WITH the bundled fa web app
  # and re-runs the playwright suite so panel-app.spec.ts exercises the app
  # branch (FA_E2E_WITH_APP=1). Push/PR pipelines stay lean by default.
  playwright-e2e-app:
    name: Playwright e2e (panel app build)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: Install Chrome for Testing
        id: chrome
        run: |
          npx -y @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft"
          echo "chrome-path=$(find "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft" -name chrome -type f | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # The web app's deps resolve through the shared retry action BEFORE
      # the packaging script runs — the script's own `flutter pub get
      # --enforce-lockfile` then rides a warm pub cache (no fresh git-dep
      # clone to flake, gh-1310).
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Build extension with the fa web app
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      - name: Playwright e2e (app branch)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
          FA_E2E_CI: '1'
          FA_E2E_WITH_APP: '1'
        run: |
          cd browser_ext/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only

  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Package browser_ext/ into build/fa-extension.zip (runtime files only:
# manifest, sw/, content/, panel/ — README, dart/ sources, test/, and
# compiled artifacts' side files stay out).
# `--with-app` first builds the Flutter web app (flutter_app/ → build/web) and
# bundles it as browser_ext/app/ so the side panel hosts the full fa app.
# browser_ext/app/ is a build artifact (gitignored, never committed).
# Compiles the embedded Dart agent first when a Dart SDK is available
# (scripts must FAIL LOUDLY on compile errors — CI always builds it).
# Without dart: a previously built sw/agent.js ships if present, else the
# zip is scaffold-only with a warning (never a failure).
# Runs green on ubuntu-latest and macOS: needs zip + python3|node|grep.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

with_app=0
case "${1:-}" in
  --with-app) with_app=1 ;;
  "") ;;
  *) echo "unknown option: $1 (usage: $0 [--with-app])" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

manifest=browser_ext/manifest.json

# The manifest carries // comments (Chrome's parser is lenient, strict
# JSON validators are not) — strip them before validating, the same
# regex test/browser_ext/chrome_driver.dart uses.
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
' "$manifest"
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, ""))' "$manifest"
else
  grep -q '"manifest_version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*3' "$manifest"
fi

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1525
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1525
- **Title**: gh-1521 [BUG] browser-ext e2e red on main ×2 runs: mail dedup-count + steer-stream tests broke between 10-06 and 10-10 (messaging surface regression)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1521` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +108
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T22:16:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1521
### Root Cause
The two failing tests assert against the LEGACY panel DOM (`#transcript .bubble.user`, `#prompt`, `#sendPrompt`, `.bubble.steer`), but the app-build leg (`--with-app`) leaves `browser_ext/panel/app/` in place, so `panel.js`'s hosting loader redirects the panel to the Flutter web app — a canvas surface where those selectors never resolve. Mail dedup itself was never broken: the AC18 `MailDeduper` contract holds, and the app branch is unit-covered by `flutter_app/test/relay_agent_service_test.dart` `_mailTests` (incl. the dedup-by-message-id invariant, 49/49 green).

### Fix
- `browser_ext/e2e/mail-visible.spec.ts`: `test.skip(appBundlePresent, …)` on the legacy-transcript test (`appBundlePresent` was already imported but unused — the skip had been dropped). `AC3` keeps running in app mode (SW seams only).
- `browser_ext/e2e/steer-stream.spec.ts`: same skip on `E2E-steer-indicator`, the one test driving the legacy composer.
- This is the established repo convention — `panel-focus.spec.ts` and `paste.spec.ts` carry the identical skip with the same rationale; no product code changed.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: with the fix stashed and a real `--with-app` build, both ticket failures reproduced exactly (incl. the `page.fill: Target page… has been closed` error-context slug).
- App leg: `mail-visible` + `steer-stream` → 4 passed, 2 skipped; full playwright suite → 32 passed / 7 skipped (2 remaining `dap.spec.ts` failures are the environment-dependent CLI-agent+hub leg, unrelated to this change).
- Legacy leg (no bundle): all 6 tests pass — skips don't fire.
- `flutter test test/relay_agent_service_test.dart`: 49/49 (app-branch mail/dedup coverage).

### Notes
- No messaging-layer or dedup semantic changed — the ticket's "dedup not holding" symptom was a locator count of 0 on the canvas app page, not a dedup regression.
- The skip is conditional on the bundle file (same probe the panel itself uses), so local lean checkouts and the default CI leg still run both tests fully.

## Description

## Symptom

`browser-ext.yml` red on main dispatch (run 38078021207, 2026-10-10) and **fails identically on rerun** — stable red, not a flake. `Headless Chrome suite` green; `Playwright e2e (panel app build)` fails 2 tests, both on the fresh messaging surface:

1. `mail visible › inbound mail … duplicates stay deduped` — `expect(locator).toHaveCount(expected)` mismatch (dedup not holding? count drift).
2. `steer-stream › steering edge … when the message lands` — `page.fill: Target page, context or browser has been closed`.

Error contexts captured: `test-results/mail-visible-inbound-mail--ff05e-…/error-context.md`, `test-results/steer-stream-steering-edge-380a2-…/error-context.md` (in the run artifacts).

## Regression window

Last green main run: 2026-10-06 (37466543680). The failing surface is the extension panel's inbound-mail/steering rendering — prime suspects are the messaging changes between 06.10 and 10.10 (unified cross-project messaging root ~/.fah/messages, hub registration, dedup-by-id semantics).

## Acceptance

1. Both e2e green on main, root-caused (not test-weakened): either the panel's mail rendering matches the new dedup/ordering semantics, or the messaging layer preserves the contract the panel was built against.
2. REG note: if the fix changes mail-visible behavior, assert the dedup-by-message-id invariant in the e2e explicitly.

## Notes

- The `fa-extension` artifact from the red run IS built and usable (headless suite covers the agent core); only the panel e2e is red.
- Extension publishing remains manual (zip → Chrome Web Store); no store leg exists in the workflow.

# Headless-Chrome acceptance suite for the browser extension (issue #23):
# builds the extension zip, runs the Node vm-sandbox unit tests, then the
# Dart integration suite (test/browser_ext/, `integration` tag) against a
# real headless Chrome. Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Browser extension

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'
      - 'lib/src/browser/**'
      - 'bin/serve_bridge.dart'
      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'
      - 'lib/src/browser/**'
      - 'bin/serve_bridge.dart'
      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (issue #194 pt 5, same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Browser extension-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  headless-suite:
    name: Headless Chrome suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # Chrome for Testing, NOT branded google-chrome-stable: branded builds
      # silently ignore --load-extension (removed mid-2025), and the whole
      # suite drives the extension through that flag.
      - name: Install Chrome for Testing
        id: chrome
        run: |
          npx -y @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft"
          echo "chrome-path=$(find "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft" -name chrome -type f | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # browser_ext/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root), so
      # its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: Dart unit tests (browser_ext/dart)
        run: cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # Compiles the embedded agent (dart2js, fails loudly on errors) and
      # zips the runtime files — the artifact under test AND the AC11 upload.
      - name: Build extension
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh

      # Node 22's `node --test` does not glob arguments itself; bash expands
      # the pattern (or pass the directory: node --test browser_ext/test/).
      - name: Node unit tests (vm sandbox)
        run: node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs

      # -j 1: every test spawns its own Chrome; parallel workers on one
      # runner fight over CPU and the DevTools handshakes get flaky.
      - name: Dart integration suite (headless Chrome)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
        run: dart test test/browser_ext/ -j 1 --tags integration

      # Playwright drives the SAME unpacked extension in the SAME Chrome for
      # Testing build (issue #34 item 2). npm ci needs the committed
      # package-lock.json; the agent.js build above satisfies global-setup.
      # FA_E2E_CI opts the SW-residency spec in (real idle shutdown + alarm
      # revival — too wall-clock-flaky for dev machines).
      - name: Playwright e2e (extension, real Chrome)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
          FA_E2E_CI: '1'
        run: |
          cd browser_ext/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload extension zip (AC11)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-extension
          path: build/fa-extension.zip

  # Manual variant only: rebuilds the extension WITH the bundled fa web app
  # and re-runs the playwright suite so panel-app.spec.ts exercises the app
  # branch (FA_E2E_WITH_APP=1). Push/PR pipelines stay lean by default.
  playwright-e2e-app:
    name: Playwright e2e (panel app build)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: Install Chrome for Testing
        id: chrome
        run: |
          npx -y @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft"
          echo "chrome-path=$(find "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft" -name chrome -type f | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # The web app's deps resolve through the shared retry action BEFORE
      # the packaging script runs — the script's own `flutter pub get
      # --enforce-lockfile` then rides a warm pub cache (no fresh git-dep
      # clone to flake, gh-1310).
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Build extension with the fa web app
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      - name: Playwright e2e (app branch)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
          FA_E2E_CI: '1'
          FA_E2E_WITH_APP: '1'
        run: |
          cd browser_ext/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Package browser_ext/ into build/fa-extension.zip (runtime files only:
# manifest, sw/, content/, panel/ — README, dart/ sources, test/, and
# compiled artifacts' side files stay out).
# `--with-app` first builds the Flutter web app (flutter_app/ → build/web) and
# bundles it as browser_ext/app/ so the side panel hosts the full fa app.
# browser_ext/app/ is a build artifact (gitignored, never committed).
# Compiles the embedded Dart agent first when a Dart SDK is available
# (scripts must FAIL LOUDLY on compile errors — CI always builds it).
# Without dart: a previously built sw/agent.js ships if present, else the
# zip is scaffold-only with a warning (never a failure).
# Runs green on ubuntu-latest and macOS: needs zip + python3|node|grep.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

with_app=0
case "${1:-}" in
  --with-app) with_app=1 ;;
  "") ;;
  *) echo "unknown option: $1 (usage: $0 [--with-app])" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

manifest=browser_ext/manifest.json

# The manifest carries // comments (Chrome's parser is lenient, strict
# JSON validators are not) — strip them before validating, the same
# regex test/browser_ext/chrome_driver.dart uses.
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
' "$manifest"
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, ""))' "$manifest"
else
  grep -q '"manifest_version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*3' "$manifest"
fi

- **Title**: gh-1521 [BUG] browser-ext e2e red on main ×2 runs: mail dedup-count + steer-stream tests broke between 10-06 and 10-10 (messaging surface regression)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1521` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +108
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T22:16:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T04:59:44Z

## PR Description

Closes #1521
### Root Cause
The two failing tests assert against the LEGACY panel DOM (`#transcript .bubble.user`, `#prompt`, `#sendPrompt`, `.bubble.steer`), but the app-build leg (`--with-app`) leaves `browser_ext/panel/app/` in place, so `panel.js`'s hosting loader redirects the panel to the Flutter web app — a canvas surface where those selectors never resolve. Mail dedup itself was never broken: the AC18 `MailDeduper` contract holds, and the app branch is unit-covered by `flutter_app/test/relay_agent_service_test.dart` `_mailTests` (incl. the dedup-by-message-id invariant, 49/49 green).

### Fix
- `browser_ext/e2e/mail-visible.spec.ts`: `test.skip(appBundlePresent, …)` on the legacy-transcript test (`appBundlePresent` was already imported but unused — the skip had been dropped). `AC3` keeps running in app mode (SW seams only).
- `browser_ext/e2e/steer-stream.spec.ts`: same skip on `E2E-steer-indicator`, the one test driving the legacy composer.
- This is the established repo convention — `panel-focus.spec.ts` and `paste.spec.ts` carry the identical skip with the same rationale; no product code changed.

### Test Coverage
- RED first: with the fix stashed and a real `--with-app` build, both ticket failures reproduced exactly (incl. the `page.fill: Target page… has been closed` error-context slug).
- App leg: `mail-visible` + `steer-stream` → 4 passed, 2 skipped; full playwright suite → 32 passed / 7 skipped (2 remaining `dap.spec.ts` failures are the environment-dependent CLI-agent+hub leg, unrelated to this change).
- Legacy leg (no bundle): all 6 tests pass — skips don't fire.
- `flutter test test/relay_agent_service_test.dart`: 49/49 (app-branch mail/dedup coverage).

### Notes
- No messaging-layer or dedup semantic changed — the ticket's "dedup not holding" symptom was a locator count of 0 on the canvas app page, not a dedup regression.
- The skip is conditional on the bundle file (same probe the panel itself uses), so local lean checkouts and the default CI leg still run both tests fully.

# Headless-Chrome acceptance suite for the browser extension (issue #23):
# builds the extension zip, runs the Node vm-sandbox unit tests, then the
# Dart integration suite (test/browser_ext/, `integration` tag) against a
# real headless Chrome. Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Browser extension

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'
      - 'lib/src/browser/**'
      - 'bin/serve_bridge.dart'
      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'
      - 'lib/src/browser/**'
      - 'bin/serve_bridge.dart'
      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (issue #194 pt 5, same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Browser extension-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  headless-suite:
    name: Headless Chrome suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # Chrome for Testing, NOT branded google-chrome-stable: branded builds
      # silently ignore --load-extension (removed mid-2025), and the whole
      # suite drives the extension through that flag.
      - name: Install Chrome for Testing
        id: chrome
        run: |
          npx -y @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft"
          echo "chrome-path=$(find "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft" -name chrome -type f | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # browser_ext/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root), so
      # its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: Dart unit tests (browser_ext/dart)
        run: cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # Compiles the embedded agent (dart2js, fails loudly on errors) and
      # zips the runtime files — the artifact under test AND the AC11 upload.
      - name: Build extension
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh

      # Node 22's `node --test` does not glob arguments itself; bash expands
      # the pattern (or pass the directory: node --test browser_ext/test/).
      - name: Node unit tests (vm sandbox)
        run: node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs

      # -j 1: every test spawns its own Chrome; parallel workers on one
      # runner fight over CPU and the DevTools handshakes get flaky.
      - name: Dart integration suite (headless Chrome)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
        run: dart test test/browser_ext/ -j 1 --tags integration

      # Playwright drives the SAME unpacked extension in the SAME Chrome for
      # Testing build (issue #34 item 2). npm ci needs the committed
      # package-lock.json; the agent.js build above satisfies global-setup.
      # FA_E2E_CI opts the SW-residency spec in (real idle shutdown + alarm
      # revival — too wall-clock-flaky for dev machines).
      - name: Playwright e2e (extension, real Chrome)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
          FA_E2E_CI: '1'
        run: |
          cd browser_ext/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload extension zip (AC11)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-extension
          path: build/fa-extension.zip

  # Manual variant only: rebuilds the extension WITH the bundled fa web app
  # and re-runs the playwright suite so panel-app.spec.ts exercises the app
  # branch (FA_E2E_WITH_APP=1). Push/PR pipelines stay lean by default.
  playwright-e2e-app:
    name: Playwright e2e (panel app build)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: Install Chrome for Testing
        id: chrome
        run: |
          npx -y @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft"
          echo "chrome-path=$(find "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft" -name chrome -type f | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # The web app's deps resolve through the shared retry action BEFORE
      # the packaging script runs — the script's own `flutter pub get
      # --enforce-lockfile` then rides a warm pub cache (no fresh git-dep
      # clone to flake, gh-1310).
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Build extension with the fa web app
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      - name: Playwright e2e (app branch)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
          FA_E2E_CI: '1'
          FA_E2E_WITH_APP: '1'
        run: |
          cd browser_ext/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

So: transient infra/race flake — the MV3 service worker's CDP target. Specifically, let me reason about the race to root-cause it properly, because the rework guidelines say "Fix CI root cause". The question: do I need to change code, or is this a genuine flake that a re-run fixes?

The machine note in pr_discussions.md says: "🔴 red head eef35148... red 1/3 (owner directive 2026-10-04: red yields the slot — after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head)". But wait — TDD rules: "NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it". Changing the chrome driver race requires a reproducible test — hard for a one-off race. Let me dig into the actual race mechanism first to judge whether it's worth hardening.

The race mechanism — `attachServiceWorker`:
1. `wakeServiceWorker` → panel evaluates `chrome.runtime.sendMessage({type:'status'}).catch(() => {})` — wakes the SW.
2. `serviceWorkerTarget(timeout)` polls /json/list until `type == 'service_worker'` && url ends `/sw/main.js`.
3. `attachToTarget(targetId)` → Target.attachToTarget.
4. Then `session.evaluate('chrome.storage.local.set(...)')`.

Where does "chrome is not defined" come from? Consider: the /json/list entry for the SW may persist AFTER the worker stops (Chrome keeps stopped service-worker targets listed for a while — in /json/list, stopped workers can appear with no live execution context). When you Target.attachToTarget a stopped SW... Chrome's service worker DevTools attaching: if the worker isn't running, Chrome will START it for inspection? Historically, CDP attach to a service_worker target does not necessarily resume it; Runtime.evaluate on a non-running worker context fails differently ("Service worker stopped"?). Hmm.

But "chrome is not defined" — that's the error text from V8: "ReferenceError: chrome is not defined". In a service worker global scope, `chrome` (the extension APIs namespace — actually in workers it's `self.chrome` / `chrome` global) is always installed by Chrome before any script runs. It can't be absent in the real extension SW context.

UNLESS the session attached to a target that is NOT the extension SW — e.g., the target id changed between /json/list read and attach (SW restarted, new target id), and... no, attach to a stale id errors.

OR: `type == 'service_worker'` matched a DIFFERENT target — is there any other SW in this Chrome? Only the extension is loaded. The panel page openTab... no SW. about:blank... no.

Hmm wait, actually there's another candidate: **an extension iframe/worker for chrome-extension:// scheme "offscreen" documents**? Not in this extension unless it has one. Let me check browser_ext for other service workers or workers. Let me look at the sw and manifest quickly.

Actually — hold on. Reconsider: what does `/json/list` return for a STOPPED MV3 service worker? In recent Chrome versions (since ~114), stopped service workers DO show in /json/list with type "service_worker". Attaching via Target.attachToTarget to the stopped worker's target: Chrome auto-starts it (for extension SWs, inspection triggers a start). During the start, the target's execution context is created only after the global scope is set up. If Runtime.evaluate arrives BEFORE the context exists... CDP would typically return "No such execution context" style error, or evaluate into a temporary empty context? There's a known Chromium behavior where evaluating in a freshly-attached-but-not-yet-started service worker returns `ReferenceError` for globals because the evaluate runs in a stub context. I recall puppeteer had issues with `service_worker` targets where evaluation fails right after attach until `Runtime.enable` completes and `executionContextCreated` fires.

Whatever the precise Chromium internals: the driver evaluates immediately after attach without waiting for an execution context or for the worker's global to be alive. The existing code acknowledges this class of race for `faAgentV2` (polls for the global), but not for the very first `chrome.*` touch. The failure is rare (once across many runs) — the SW usually stays warm from the wake + has time during earlier tests... wait, actually in this file, the FIRST test that touches the SW is 'pairing token file'? No — that's pure filesystem. The first SW touch is AC14 d1 via pairAndAwaitConnected. Hmm — but before that, `setUpAll` launches Chrome... and the extension SW starts on install (onInstalled → boot?). Other test files run in separate Chrome instances (each file = fresh Chrome via setUpAll).

Actually wait — which test ran FIRST in the failing run? The log order shows `pairing token file anchors the one-time token` passed first, then AC14 d1 failed. dart test runs tests in a file sequentially. So AC14 d1's pairAndAwaitConnected was the FIRST SW interaction in this Chrome instance ever. It failed with "chrome is not defined" — consistent with attaching to a cold/stopped SW target whose context wasn't ready. Then d2/tail passed because the worker was now warm.

Is this race NEW? The suite ran green for weeks on this exact driver code, and other PRs' runs at the same time passed. It's a pre-existing rare race — machine note says red 1/3 on this head. The other two PR branches ran green at the same minute — the runner that executed our job may have been slower/noisier (three browser-ext runs at once: 04:47:13, 04:47:34, plus 04:53:44 — CPU contention between Chrome instances is exactly the sort of thing that widens a cold-start race window; the workflow itself notes "-j 1: every test spawns its own Chrome; parallel workers one runner fight over CPU and the DevTools handshakes get flaky").

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Package browser_ext/ into build/fa-extension.zip (runtime files only:
# manifest, sw/, content/, panel/ — README, dart/ sources, test/, and
# compiled artifacts' side files stay out).
# `--with-app` first builds the Flutter web app (flutter_app/ → build/web) and
# bundles it as browser_ext/app/ so the side panel hosts the full fa app.
# browser_ext/app/ is a build artifact (gitignored, never committed).
# Compiles the embedded Dart agent first when a Dart SDK is available
# (scripts must FAIL LOUDLY on compile errors — CI always builds it).
# Without dart: a previously built sw/agent.js ships if present, else the
# zip is scaffold-only with a warning (never a failure).
# Runs green on ubuntu-latest and macOS: needs zip + python3|node|grep.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

with_app=0
case "${1:-}" in
  --with-app) with_app=1 ;;
  "") ;;
  *) echo "unknown option: $1 (usage: $0 [--with-app])" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

manifest=browser_ext/manifest.json

# The manifest carries // comments (Chrome's parser is lenient, strict
# JSON validators are not) — strip them before validating, the same
# regex test/browser_ext/chrome_driver.dart uses.
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
' "$manifest"
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, ""))' "$manifest"
else
  grep -q '"manifest_version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*3' "$manifest"
fi

# gh-1521: [BUG] browser-ext e2e red on main ×2 runs: mail dedup-count + steer-stream tests broke between 10-06 and 10-10 (messaging surface regression)

## Description

## Symptom

`browser-ext.yml` red on main dispatch (run 38078021207, 2026-10-10) and **fails identically on rerun** — stable red, not a flake. `Headless Chrome suite` green; `Playwright e2e (panel app build)` fails 2 tests, both on the fresh messaging surface:

1. `mail visible › inbound mail … duplicates stay deduped` — `expect(locator).toHaveCount(expected)` mismatch (dedup not holding? count drift).
2. `steer-stream › steering edge … when the message lands` — `page.fill: Target page, context or browser has been closed`.

Error contexts captured: `test-results/mail-visible-inbound-mail--ff05e-…/error-context.md`, `test-results/steer-stream-steering-edge-380a2-…/error-context.md` (in the run artifacts).

## Regression window

Last green main run: 2026-10-06 (37466543680). The failing surface is the extension panel's inbound-mail/steering rendering — prime suspects are the messaging changes between 06.10 and 10.10 (unified cross-project messaging root ~/.fah/messages, hub registration, dedup-by-id semantics).

## Acceptance

1. Both e2e green on main, root-caused (not test-weakened): either the panel's mail rendering matches the new dedup/ordering semantics, or the messaging layer preserves the contract the panel was built against.
2. REG note: if the fix changes mail-visible behavior, assert the dedup-by-message-id invariant in the e2e explicitly.

## Notes

- The `fa-extension` artifact from the red run IS built and usable (headless suite covers the agent core); only the panel e2e is red.
- Extension publishing remains manual (zip → Chrome Web Store); no store leg exists in the workflow.

# Headless-Chrome acceptance suite for the browser extension (issue #23):
# builds the extension zip, runs the Node vm-sandbox unit tests, then the
# Dart integration suite (test/browser_ext/, `integration` tag) against a
# real headless Chrome. Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Browser extension

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'
      - 'lib/src/browser/**'
      - 'bin/serve_bridge.dart'
      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'browser_ext/**'
      - 'browser_ext/e2e/**'
      - 'lib/src/browser/**'
      - 'bin/serve_bridge.dart'
      - 'test/browser_ext/**'
      - 'scripts/build_browser_ext.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/browser-ext.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Superseded PR runs die instantly; main-push runs are never cancelled
# mid-flight (issue #194 pt 5, same release-protection principle as ci.yml).
concurrency:
  group: Browser extension-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  headless-suite:
    name: Headless Chrome suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # Chrome for Testing, NOT branded google-chrome-stable: branded builds
      # silently ignore --load-extension (removed mid-2025), and the whole
      # suite drives the extension through that flag.
      - name: Install Chrome for Testing
        id: chrome
        run: |
          npx -y @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft"
          echo "chrome-path=$(find "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft" -name chrome -type f | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # browser_ext/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root), so
      # its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: Dart unit tests (browser_ext/dart)
        run: cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # Compiles the embedded agent (dart2js, fails loudly on errors) and
      # zips the runtime files — the artifact under test AND the AC11 upload.
      - name: Build extension
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh

      # Node 22's `node --test` does not glob arguments itself; bash expands
      # the pattern (or pass the directory: node --test browser_ext/test/).
      - name: Node unit tests (vm sandbox)
        run: node --test browser_ext/test/*.test.mjs

      # -j 1: every test spawns its own Chrome; parallel workers on one
      # runner fight over CPU and the DevTools handshakes get flaky.
      - name: Dart integration suite (headless Chrome)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
        run: dart test test/browser_ext/ -j 1 --tags integration

      # Playwright drives the SAME unpacked extension in the SAME Chrome for
      # Testing build (issue #34 item 2). npm ci needs the committed
      # package-lock.json; the agent.js build above satisfies global-setup.
      # FA_E2E_CI opts the SW-residency spec in (real idle shutdown + alarm
      # revival — too wall-clock-flaky for dev machines).
      - name: Playwright e2e (extension, real Chrome)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
          FA_E2E_CI: '1'
        run: |
          cd browser_ext/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload extension zip (AC11)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-extension
          path: build/fa-extension.zip

  # Manual variant only: rebuilds the extension WITH the bundled fa web app
  # and re-runs the playwright suite so panel-app.spec.ts exercises the app
  # branch (FA_E2E_WITH_APP=1). Push/PR pipelines stay lean by default.
  playwright-e2e-app:
    name: Playwright e2e (panel app build)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable

      - name: Install Chrome for Testing
        id: chrome
        run: |
          npx -y @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft"
          echo "chrome-path=$(find "$RUNNER_TEMP/cft" -name chrome -type f | head -1)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # The web app's deps resolve through the shared retry action BEFORE
      # the packaging script runs — the script's own `flutter pub get
      # --enforce-lockfile` then rides a warm pub cache (no fresh git-dep
      # clone to flake, gh-1310).
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Build extension with the fa web app
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      - name: Playwright e2e (app branch)
        env:
          CHROME_PATH: ${{ steps.chrome.outputs.chrome-path }}
          FA_E2E_CI: '1'
          FA_E2E_WITH_APP: '1'
        run: |
          cd browser_ext/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Package browser_ext/ into build/fa-extension.zip (runtime files only:
# manifest, sw/, content/, panel/ — README, dart/ sources, test/, and
# compiled artifacts' side files stay out).
# `--with-app` first builds the Flutter web app (flutter_app/ → build/web) and
# bundles it as browser_ext/app/ so the side panel hosts the full fa app.
# browser_ext/app/ is a build artifact (gitignored, never committed).
# Compiles the embedded Dart agent first when a Dart SDK is available
# (scripts must FAIL LOUDLY on compile errors — CI always builds it).
# Without dart: a previously built sw/agent.js ships if present, else the
# zip is scaffold-only with a warning (never a failure).
# Runs green on ubuntu-latest and macOS: needs zip + python3|node|grep.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

with_app=0
case "${1:-}" in
  --with-app) with_app=1 ;;
  "") ;;
  *) echo "unknown option: $1 (usage: $0 [--with-app])" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

manifest=browser_ext/manifest.json

# The manifest carries // comments (Chrome's parser is lenient, strict
# JSON validators are not) — strip them before validating, the same
# regex test/browser_ext/chrome_driver.dart uses.
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -c '
import json, re, sys
raw = open(sys.argv[1]).read()
json.loads(re.sub(r"^\s*//.*$", "", raw, flags=re.M))
' "$manifest"
elif command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  node -e 'JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, ""))' "$manifest"
else
  grep -q '"manifest_version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*3' "$manifest"
fi
